lessons.title: Ideas Are Easy, Execution Is Everything
lessons.key_idea: Most organizations fail not from bad ideas but from poor execution, and Doerr brought OKRs to an early Google to fix exactly that.

lessons.title: What an OKR Actually Is
lessons.key_idea: An objective says what you want to achieve, and a few measurable key results say how you will know you got there, a method Andy Grove built at Intel.

lessons.title: Focus and Commit to Few Priorities
lessons.key_idea: Choosing only a handful of objectives forces hard choices about what matters most, as Intel did when it rallied the whole company around Operation Crush.
issues: scene 6: The dashed growth curve starts right at the end of the 'PICKED INTEL FOR ITS FIRST PC' caption and touches it, so the line and the caption collide. The 'SHAPED INTEL FOR DECADES' label also sits detached below the curve's starting point instead of reading as the curve's label. (fix: Move the curve's starting point at least 40px right of and below the IBM caption so it no longer touches the text. Place 'SHAPED INTEL FOR DECADES' beside the upper part of the curve, near the arrowhead, so it clearly labels the trajectory.)

lessons.title: Align and Connect in the Open
lessons.key_idea: Making everyone's OKRs public, and letting goals flow both from leaders and from front-line teams, keeps an organization pulling in the same direction.

lessons.title: Track Progress and Stay Accountable
lessons.key_idea: Regular check-ins, honest scoring and a willingness to adjust or drop goals turn OKRs into a living tool rather than a forgotten plan.
issues: scene 4: The indigo strikethrough on OBJECTIVE B runs straight through the rotated 'STOPPED' stamp, so the line cuts across the stamp's text and makes it hard to read. (fix: End the strikethrough before the stamp. Alternatively, move the stamp to the right end of the row, give it an opaque stage-colour fill, and draw it above the strike line so its text stays clear.)

lessons.title: Stretch for Amazing Goals
lessons.key_idea: Separating committed goals from aspirational stretch goals pushes teams beyond what feels possible, as YouTube did by aiming for a billion hours of daily watch time.

lessons.title: Conversations, Feedback and Recognition Complete It
lessons.key_idea: OKRs work best alongside ongoing conversations, feedback and recognition, which together build a culture where clear goals and real support drive great results.

plan.title: Measure What Matters
plan.author: John Doerr
plan.confidence_note: I know this book's core framework, its main arguments and several of its well-known case studies in detail, though not every company story verbatim.
plan.one_liner: The simple goal-setting system that helped Intel and Google turn big ambitions into measurable results.
plan.summary: Venture capitalist John Doerr explains Objectives and Key Results, or OKRs, a goal-setting method he learned from Andy Grove at Intel in the 1970s and later introduced to a young Google. An objective is what you want to achieve. Key results are the measurable steps that show whether you are getting there. Doerr argues that OKRs give organizations four superpowers. They help teams focus on what matters most, align everyone's work in the open, track progress honestly and stretch toward ambitious goals. Through stories from Intel, Google, YouTube, nonprofits and startups, he shows the system in action. He then pairs OKRs with continuous conversations, feedback and recognition, which replace the dreaded annual review. The message is that ideas are easy, execution is everything, and clear, shared, measurable goals are how good execution happens.
